entries.title: Photos: Chicago Marathon draws thousands of runners from around the world
entries.summary: <p>Tens of thousands of Chicago Marathon runners started their hours-long journey on foot as the sun rose over North Columbus Drive in Grant Park. What waited for them ahead were 26.2 miles of some of Chicago's most distinct neighborhoods— from the Loop to Wrigleyville, down to the Near West Side, Pilsen, Bronzeville and Chinatown — and thousands of people cheering them on.</p><p>Ruby Reducindo, who was dressed as a pink cow holding a sign reading "Mooove" was one of the spectators eagerly looking for her sister in the crowd.</p><p>"I feel emotional and very proud and motivated every time," she said as she teared up. "She motivates me a lot in life, and she's doing so many hard things and then I'm just here to cheer her on."</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> entries.title: Bears coach Ben Johnson runs out of answers, unable to ignite offense in 31-7 loss to Packers
entries.summary: <p>GREEN BAY, Wis. — For the first time since his very early days coaching <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >the Bears</a>, Ben Johnson looked like he was out of answers Sunday against the Packers.</p><p>Backup quarterback Tyson Bagent couldn’t get anything going, so Johnson tried Case Keenum in the fourth quarter. Nothing. The rushing attack never found a groove. No one stepped up as a go-to option in the passing game.</p><p>Play after play failed, and the Packers crushed the Bears 31-7 at Lambeau Field. It was the most lopsided and embarrassing loss for Johnson since the Lions ran him out of the building in his second game last season.</p><p>‘‘When you can’t get in a rhythm offensively, I’ve got to look at myself first,’’ Johnson said. ‘‘What do we have in? Did we prepare the right way? What [were] the play-calls?’’</p><p>Johnson credited Packers defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon for having his number all day and said, ‘‘We knew we were going to get their best shot, and we sure did.’’ But he still was frustrated that his team undermined itself with errors.</p><p>It was the Bears’ first game since <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/09/1985-bears-championship-team-remembers-former-coach-mike-ditka-as-tip-of-the-spear" target="_blank" >the death Friday of former coach Mike Ditka</a>, and players wore a No. 89 decal on their helmets in honor of the number he wore as a Bears tight end in the 1960s. The Packers held a moment of silence for Ditka before the game.</p><p>Johnson immersed himself in this rivalry with his ‘‘[Expletive] the Packers’’ rant last season and by exchanging snippy shots with coach Matt LaFleur, but there was none of that after this one. He and LaFleur met briefly afterward, and Johnson appeared to say, ‘‘Good job,’’ while shaking LaFleur’s hand with a grimace.</p><p>He must have thought his team was beyond something this ugly, even with a backup quarterback. This is the same coach who felt emboldened enough to set his sights on the 2013 Broncos’ single-season scoring record and a trip to the Super Bowl.</p><p>Who could deny him after the Bears opened with 59 points against the Panthers? They’ve totaled 60 in four games since then, however, and they now would need to average nearly 44 a game to set the record.</p><p>That’s overly ambitious, even with the possibility of quarterback Caleb Williams returning Sunday against the Falcons.</p><p>A week earlier, when Bagent was mediocre against the Jets, No. 2 running back Kyle Monangai was the engine of the offense with 146 yards rushing and two touchdowns. He missed the game against the Packers with a toe injury, and no one else showed up to save the day. Bagent completed 12 of 21 passes for 87 yards with two interceptions for a 27.4 passer rating before Johnson benched him.</p><p>‘‘Super-disappointed but really can’t look any further than the mirror,’’ Bagent said. ‘‘It really, starting with me, just didn’t go our way.’’</p><p>There was a flicker late in the third quarter when Bagent connected with tight end Colston Loveland for a seven-yard pass on fourth-and-four with the Bears down 23-7, but he threw an interception on the next play. Gannon fooled Bagent by showing a Cover 0 defense (no safety deep) before the snap, then the Packers flipped to a Cover 2 and had safety Xavier McKinney in perfect position to beat Loveland to the ball for his second pick of the game.</p><p>Keenum was no better. He walked into a golden opportunity at the Packers’ 31-yard line and threw an interception in the end zone on fourth-and-goal. He also lost a fumble and finished 11-for-19 for 108 yards and a 52.1 rating.</p><p>Unwilling to concede, Johnson kept swinging to the end and had Keenum throw deep on fourth-and-21 from his own 21-yard line with 1:10 left.</p><p>A week after running an NFL-season-high 89 plays and racking up 492 yards in a punt-free victory against the Jets, the Bears managed only 246 yards against the Packers — their fewest under Johnson — and went 4-for-14 on third down.</p><p>That reheated the debate about whether Johnson should have stuck with Keenum, who lit up the Eagles in the Bears’ first game after Williams’ hamstring injury. Johnson wouldn’t say whom he would start against the Falcons if Williams remains out.</p><p>The Bears need everything Williams brings: dual-threat playmaking, improvisational wizardry and electric energy. Johnson has managed his absence in the short term, and it’s not the end of the world to sit 3-2 with Williams on the verge of coming back. But Johnson’s playbook alone can’t carry the Bears for the long run.</p><p>Williams progressed from throwing on the side last week to practicing partially Friday to working out at Lambeau Field before the game. He appears to be on track to step back into his spot at practice Wednesday, but when Johnson was asked about him playing against the Falcons, he said, ‘‘It’s going to be close.’’</p><p>If there’s anything uncertain about Williams’ health, it would be prudent for the Bears to hold him out until a game against the Patriots the following Thursday. Two games in five days might not be ideal for Williams coming off his injury, and the Bears will have an extended break after the game against the Patriots leading up to their visit Nov. 2 to the defending champion Seahawks.</p><p>But for whatever amount of time the Bears have to wait for Williams, it’s on Johnson to figure out a solution. His ability to adjust and pivot has been his hallmark as the Bears’ coach, but he ran out of moves Sunday.</p>
entries.author: Jason Lieser

entries.title: Bears' post-Ditka-era misery at Lambeau Field resumes as Packers revel in 31-7 beatdown
entries.summary: <p>GREEN BAY, Wis. — Well, that was a real kick in the keister.</p><p>“Green Bay sucks,” does it?</p><p>Chicago sports fans can chant that until they’re blue in the face. <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> coach Ben Johnson can “hate” the bleepin’ Packers all he wants. Anyone still pointing to the Bears’ two wins in this rivalry last season, the second one coming in the playoffs, can knock themselves out.</p><p>But we all just saw the same thing — a <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/11/packers-lead-bears-14-7-at-halftime-at-lambeau-field-after-costly-tyson-bagent-interception" target="_blank" >31-7 Packers beatdown of the Bears</a> that might as well have been by 100 points.</p><p>Maybe Mike Ditka saw it too. Imagine what the Bears coach who made Lambeau Field his personal playground would’ve thought about his old team’s no-show performance.</p><p>The Packers rubbed the Bears’ faces in the dirt. Their coach, Matt LaFleur, took Johnson’s lunch money, gave him a swirly and stuffed him in a locker. The better team out of these two? Please. The 3-2 records might be the same, but it isn’t even close.</p><p>Perhaps Johnson sensed it when he said at halftime to ESPN 1000 sideline reporter Jason McKie, “We gotta play f——ng better. We gotta be f——ng better.” Then again, the Bears trailed just 14-7 at the time and still had four second-half turnovers to commit and loads of long completions by the Packers to suffer through.</p><p>Who knew Packers quarterback Jordan Love (25 of 31 for 367 yards and two touchdowns) was better than Bart Starr, Brett Favre or Aaron Rodgers? Who knew receivers Christian Watson (six catches, 143 yards, two touchdowns) and Matthew Golden (six catches, 123 yards) put Don Hutson, Sterling Sharpe and Donald Driver to shame? Who knew safety Xavier McKinney (two interceptions) should have his name immortalized on the Lambeau facade instead of LeRoy Butler?</p><p>Or maybe they were all just lucky to be toying with the Bears on a miserable day for the visitors.</p><p>“That was a great display that we had out there,” Watson said, puffed with rivalry pride. “It definitely felt a little extra.”</p><p>“I’m not gonna say it wasn’t big for us,” McKinney said. “I’m not gonna say we didn’t have the intensity and the urgency this whole week knowing [whom] our opponent was going to be.”</p><p>Ditka lost his first game here as Bears coach, in 1983. After that, it went completely the other way, Ditka’s teams winning eight of nine while one Packers offense after another could barely score. Even his last team, in 1992, blew out the Packers 30-10 at Lambeau, raising the Bears’ record to 4-3.</p><p>“Let me tell you something here,” Ditka said that day. “If we keep improving like we are, we have a chance to make something happen.”</p><p>Yeah, well, no. Those Bears ended up 5-11 and Ditka got fired. But then the Packers won 12 of the next 13 games, and 20 of the next 23, head-to-head. At Lambeau, the Bears are a pathetic 9-25 since the Ditka era.</p><p>“Got to love the excitement around the rivalry and all that,” LaFleur said, his record against the Bears — 13-2 — looking mighty impressive.</p><p>And the beatdowns go on.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" > <div class="TweetUrl"> <blockquote class="twitter-tweet"><p lang="en" dir="ltr">Packers hold a moment of silence for Mike Ditka at Lambeau Field before today’s game— <a href="https://t.co/DiItnliVxh">pic.twitter.com/DiItnliVxh</a></p>— Jason Lieser (@JasonLieser) <a href="https://x.com/JasonLieser/status/2109328562616496332?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw">October 11, 2026</a></blockquote> <script async src="https://platform.x.com/widgets.js" charset="utf-8"></script> </div> </div> </div></div><p></p><h3></h3><p></p><p></p><p></p><p></p><p></p><p></p><p></p><p></p><p></p><p></p><p></p><h3><b>TOMORROW’S HEADLINES</b></h3><p><b>A Caleb Comeback? </b>Williams could return for the Bears’ next game, in Atlanta on Sunday — otherwise known as not a minute too soon.</p><p><b>Bagent or Keenum? </b>Somebody has to be QB2 on this team — and maybe even the starter against the Falcons. Bagent was bad enough to be knocked down a peg, but will he be?</p><p><b>Defense in Disarray: </b>The Bears have serious coverage issues, especially if they can’t rely on having more of a pass rush. entries.title: Bears' grades vs. Packers are in. How did they do in Green Bay?
entries.summary: <p>GREEN BAY, Wis. — Well, that was a real kick in the kiester.</p><p>The best thing about the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" >Bears’</a> 31-7 loss to the Packers at Lambeau Field? It's over.</p><p>The worst thing? Seriously, who could pick?</p><h3><b>QUARTERBACKS — F</b></h3><p>Remember that hilarious narrative about the Bears having not one, not two, but three good players at the most important position in all of sports? Man, <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/11/bears-bench-qb-tyson-bagent-after-two-interceptions-vs-packers-then-case-keenum-throws-one-too" >what a hoot that was.</a> It’s hard to guess what Tyson Bagent spent the previous week doing, but it can’t have been preparing to face the Packers. Even when he wasn’t gifting the ball to Packers safety Xavier McKinney — one interception thrown smack into double coverage, the other thrown behind Colston Loveland — he was off target and anything but in command. Case Keenum came in for the fourth quarter and promptly added a pick to the Packers’ pile, and later lost a fumble. Where you at, Caleb Williams? Your services are desperately needed.</p><h3><b>DEFENSIVE BACKS — F</b></h3><p>Somewhere along the way, Packers QB Jordan Love found wide receiver Christian Watson for a 31-yard gain. The point? Hard to believe this could happen, but it was merely Love’s <i>sixth</i>-longest pass of the game. Xavier Woods got spun like a top on Watson’s 42-yard touchdown to open the scoring. Dillon Thieneman was inside Watson’s jersey on a 53-yard touchdown yet somehow failed to make any play on the ball whatsoever. Malik Muhammad got torched on a 46-yarder to tight end Tucker Kraft. Jaylon Johnson gave up his share of big ones — is he fast enough anymore? — and got absolutely run over by MarShawn Lloyd on the running back’s six-yard touchdown rumble.</p><h3><b>DEFENSIVE LINE — D-PLUS</b></h3><p>Here’s looking at you, Austin Booker, you two-sack haver, you. Alas, nobody else got after Love or else he wouldn’t have had time to luxuriate in the pocket before chucking all those long balls. Pretty sure Love was spotted sipping from an umbrella drink before one of the heaves.</p><h3><b>SPECIAL TEAMS — C</b></h3><p>File Zavion Thomas’ 61-yard kickoff return in the back of your head; at some point this season, he’ll bust a big one that’ll really mean something. Cairo Santos was wide left on a 43-yard field-goal attempt, which didn’t mean much by the end a miserable day for the team but kept the Bears from closing to 20-10 — which wouldn’t have seemed hopeless at the time.</p><h3><b>COACHING — F</b></h3><p>Western scholars will ruminate for many years on which was worse Sunday, the Bears’ offense or their defense. But this was all kinds of awful. Ben Johnson can hate the Packers all he wants, but they still tortured him on what had to be the worst day of his head coaching life. The Bears were unprepared. They made a million bad mistakes. What an embarrassing display.</p>

entries.title: White Sox express hope amid sadness, but they know next season won't be the same
entries.summary: <p>CLEVELAND — The visitors’ clubhouse at Progressive Field wasn’t filled with despair after the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" target="_blank" >White Sox</a>’ loss Saturday night.</p><p>There certainly was sadness after the team lost its third consecutive game and let the Guardians off the hook after they had dropped the first two in the American League Division Series. But there were lots of hugs and handshakes and enough smiles to belie the feeling.</p><p>‘‘More to come,’’ an optimistic Davis Martin was overheard saying.</p><p>Sean Burke took an undeserved loss in Game 5, allowing the only runs on a two-run home run by Jose Ramirez, who hit a pitch that was almost in the dirt. That didn’t stop Burke from going person to person in the clubhouse, thanking, consoling and congratulating teammates, whichever fit the moment.</p><p>‘‘These are my brothers,’’ Burke said. ‘‘I’ve played on a lot of teams in my life. This is definitely my favorite team I’ve ever played on.’’</p><p>Miguel Vargas, who led the Sox by far with a 1.129 OPS in the series, felt the same way, making the end of the season harder to swallow.</p><p>‘‘We just love each other so much in this clubhouse,’’ he said. ‘‘It’s not going to be the same next year, for sure.’’</p><p>Indeed, it won’t. It never is. Though much of the Sox’ young core figures to return, there are few guarantees. Some highly respected veterans, such as Erick Fedde and Randal Grichuk, probably won’t be back, and some highly rated prospects, such as Caleb Bonemer and Roch Cholowsky, could join the team. It might be great, but it won’t be this.</p><p>‘‘It was a pretty unique group,’’ Grant Taylor said. ‘‘The contributions we had to the clubhouse, even from guys that weren’t on the field, like [injured] Mike Vasil, everyday guys, just having a good time. We were friends, which is not what you get out of a clubhouse a lot of times.’’</p><p>‘‘This is so different than last year for us,’’ said Chase Meidroth, referring to the third of three consecutive seasons with more than 100 losses. ‘‘This is a family; this is a brotherhood. We wanted to win for each other. I didn’t love baseball like this last year.’’</p><div class="RelatedList Enhancement" data-module data-align-center> <div class="RelatedList-title">Related</div> <ul class="RelatedList-items"> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/10/10/sean-burke-chicago-white-sox-chris-getz-will-venable-cleveland-guardians-mlb-postseason-playoffs-starting-pitching" >Sean Burke gives White Sox what they’ve been missing — and need more of</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/10/11/the-white-sox-offense-powered-their-rise-and-its-holes-hastened-their-demise-munetaka-murakami" >The White Sox’ offense powered their rise, and its holes hastened their demise</a> </li> <li class="RelatedList-items-item"> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox/2026/10/10/optimistic-white-sox-fans-fill-ramova-theatre-for-alds-winner-take-all-watch-party" >White Sox playoff run ends in a ‘bummer,’ but South Side fans cherish unexpected ride</a> </li> </ul> </div> <p>That was evident in the clubhouse after the game. Though the Sox struck out 21 times, setting the MLB record for strikeouts in a nine-inning game — postseason or regular season — there was some positivity and a feeling of ‘‘We showed you’’ amid some teary eyes and raw emotions.</p><p>‘‘We proved we’re a good team,’’ Burke said. ‘‘We believed throughout the season when people were doubting us and said this wasn’t sustainable or this was a fluke. More importantly, we proved to ourselves that we can do this.’’</p><p>‘‘Starting from last year in the second half, we all believed that we could be a winning playoff team,’’ Colson Montgomery said. ‘‘And we carried that mentality into this year.’’</p><p>‘‘We stuck together,’’ Vargas said. ‘‘The vibes in the clubhouse, everything was so awesome, sharing the time with the guys this year. We created a brotherhood here that is going to be forever. It’s a tough one, but it’s just the beginning for us.’’</p><p>Those who expect to be back expect to be better.</p><p>‘‘I’m still swinging at the high-velocity pitches and breaking balls down, and the chase is there,’’ Munetaka Murakami said through a translator. ‘‘So I’ve got to be better in all the mechanics and all the aspects of baseball.’’</p><p>‘‘Get better next year; we’ll be ready,’’ Meidroth said. ‘‘Being here [was a] good experience for next year, coming to camp and knowing what you need to do to get where we’re at today.’’</p><p>‘‘Obviously, not the result we hoped for in this series, but this core will be together for a little bit,’’ Burke said. ‘‘As sad as it is now that the season’s over, there’s so many bright spots to look forward to and such a good future to look forward to for the White Sox.’’</p><p>Sox fans have heard that before, and it has led to anything but. Team history is littered with one-offs. In 126 seasons, the Sox have made consecutive postseason appearances once, in 2020-21, and the first season was shortened by the pandemic.</p><p>It sounds as though these Sox expect to make it two.</p><p>‘‘We’ll be back next year,’’ Meidroth said, ‘‘and this group will keep getting stronger.’’</p><p>‘‘We know we probably should’ve got the job done,’’ Montgomery said, ‘‘but you’ve got to take away what we did this year. There’s a lot to be proud of.’’</p>

entries.title: Center of attention for shrinking Bulls as they fall in Denver 133-128
entries.summary: <p>One glance around the Advocate Center a few weeks ago and it was almost like Matas Buzelis was re-invigorated.</p><p>The Bulls forward had spent most of September running in open gyms with his teammates and now that camp was underway and the Tiago Splitter playbook was being installed, Buzelis was reminded of his new-look roster.</p><p>“I remember walking in (the other day), and I was just looking around like, ‘Man, we’re pretty big.’ “ Buzelis said. “We’ve got a lot of fours, guys that can make plays, athleticism. That just makes you more comfortable defensively.”</p><p>The NBA can be cruel at times.</p><p>The Bulls went into their third preseason game in Denver on Sunday night not big at all. They came out on the other side of the 133-128 loss begging for some size to return, especially in the middle.</p><p>Nic Claxton was still working through a hamstring issue that could cost him a few regular-season games out of the gate, Zach Collins has been dealing with a sore quadriceps, and then Jalen Smith aggravated his foot before the loss to Memphis on Friday, missed the game, but returned against the Nuggets.</p><p>The problem in this game of musical chairs, however, is while Smith was back, impressive rookie rebounding machine Tobe Awaka was now out, dealing with a sore knee that was considered day-to-day.</p><p>That’s the Bulls missing just under 21 feet of bodies to protect the rim.</p><p>That’s a problem.</p><p>“It is a concern,” Splitter said of his bigs already spending more time in the training room than on the court for preseason action.</p><p>Especially because the coach has one underlying philosophy in common with former coach Billy Donovan and that’s run, run and run some more on the offensive side of the ball.</p><p>“We’ve got to be careful with their minutes throughout the season,” Splitter said of the centers. “We’ll probably have to have every night a three-man rotation at the five position. It’s a little bit also what the league is now playing physical, fast. Seven footers can’t play for 35 minutes so you have to divide those minutes with three big men running up and down.”</p><p>That means having Claxton, Collins and Smith up and running as soon as possible, with Awaka waiting in the wings as the insurance policy. Another option, however, could be rookie Caleb Wilson who played the five at North Carolina and is versatile enough to guard smaller fives.</p><p>“The game is really transitioning right now so I don’t want to box myself into a role,” Wilson said when asked if he could was more of a three, four or a five.</p><p>He did eventually settle on being more of a three right now at the NBA level but was open to do whatever was asked.</p><p>The ask was large for not only Wilson but all the Bulls starters against Denver, especially with the Nuggets starting perennial league-MVP finalist Nikola Jokic (6-foot-11) and ultra-athletic forward Aaron Gordon.</p><p>All Jokic did in his first seven-plus minutes of work in that opening quarter was score 10 points on 4-of-4 shooting, finishing with a triple-double with 22 points, 11 rebounds and 10 assists, while Gordon chipped in 25 points.</p><p>The visiting team did hang in there on the scoreboard most of the night, including in the opening stanza against most of Denver’s starters. It was obvious from the jump, however, where the Nuggets wanted to attack, outscoring the Bulls 16-8 in the paint in the first stanza.</p><p>The Bulls’ second unit did smooth those numbers out a bit, especially in using an up-tempo approach to try and negate the size. That meant more solid showings by the frontcourt players, led by Leonard Miller’s 26 points, while Wilson had 17 and Buzelis 13.</p><p>The good news for the Bulls is Collins continued getting closer to a return with two preseason games left and the early indications were Awaka would also be back by the Wednesday game in Milwaukee.</p>

entries.title: Halloween shopping trip turns deadly for woman, 22, shot in Little Village
entries.summary: <p>A 22-year-old woman who was fatally shot Saturday night after getting home from shopping for Halloween supplies with her mom in Little Village, has been identified, officials said. </p><p>Abbygail Somoza was standing on a street along the 2800 block of West 23rd Street around 8:43 p.m. when she reported hearing a loud noise and later feeling pain, police said. </p><p>Somoza, of the 2800 b lock of West 23rd Place, was transported by ambulance to Mount Sinai Hospital and was listed in critical condition with a gunshot wound to the armpit before later dying, police said. </p><p>Somoza and her mother had just returned home from shopping for Halloween supplies when shots rang out from about a block away and Somoza was hit, according to a police report obtained by the Sun-Times. Her mother was not injured.</p><p>A Sunday autopsy determined Somoza died of a gunshot wound to the torso, according to the Cook County medical examiner's office. Her death was ruled a homicide.</p><p>Area 4 detectives are investigating.<br></p>
entries.author: Sun-Times Wire

entries.title: Woman, 21, sexually assaulted at frat house near the University of Chicago in Hyde Park
entries.summary: <p>Chicago police are investigating the sexual assault of a 21-year-old woman at a frat house near the University of Chicago in Hyde Park early Sunday, according to Chicago police and the university newspaper. </p><p>The woman told officers the assault happened around 2 a.m. Sunday in the 5600 block of South University Avenue, Chicago police said. </p><p>The assault allegedly happened at the house of the Lambda chapter of the Alpha Epsilon Pi (AEPi) fraternity, according to the university's <a class="Link" href="https://chicagomaroon.com/53960/news/sexual-assault-reported-at-aepi-fraternity-house/" target="_blank" >student newspaper</a>. </p><p>She went to the University of Chicago Medical Center for treatment, police said. </p><p>The student paper reported that the woman isn't a student. </p><p>Area 1 detectives were investigating. </p>
entries.author: Sun-Times Wire

entries.title: Girl, 14, shot in calf at Northwest Side home
entries.summary: <p>A 14-year-old girl was recovering in fair condition after she was shot in the leg early Monday in a home on the Northwest Side. </p><p>Around 3 a.m., officers responded to a person shot in the 3100 block of North Kolmar Avenue and found the girl shot in the calf, Chicago police said. </p><p>She was taken to Advocate Illinois Masonic Medical Center in fair condition, police said. </p><p>Area 5 detectives were investigating. </p>

entries.title: Dear Abby: Campaign sign leads to marital strife
entries.summary: <p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> I went out to run errands, and when I returned home, I found a political sign in our front yard. It seems a candidate asked my husband for a pledge of support, and he agreed to place the sign in our front yard without consulting me.</p><p>Because of my job, I have always stayed neutral and never publicly endorsed any candidate for political office. When I expressed concern, my husband laughed at me and told our son, "Mom is worried what others will think." The issue is that I do not wish to publicly endorse any candidate, and neighbors will assume the person is someone we both endorse (which is not true at all).</p><p>Is this a form of passive-aggression on my husband's part, displaying his lack of respect for my privacy? Am I wrong to believe that he has failed to respect the fact that we are a couple? Had he discussed his desire to show support, I would have suggested he wear a button or place a bumper sticker on his personal vehicle. Instead, he placed a sign in front of our house! — <i>FUMING IN PENNSYLVANIA</i></p><p><b>DEAR FUMING:</b> Your husband's unilateral decision to allow the candidate to plant his sign on your lawn may have been made on impulse, without thinking it through. However, for him to have laughed and made light of your concern in front of your son was disrespectful.</p><p>In the state where I live, several individuals have confided that clients had made them feel — or told them directly — that if they knew they had voted for a different candidate, they would no longer employ them.</p><p>Does your husband act unilaterally or belittle you in front of your son when other disagreements arise? If so, you may need to discuss your relationship problem with a licensed marriage and family therapist.</p><p><b>DEAR ABBY:</b> My daughter is getting married soon. I purchased my dress for the wedding and sent a picture of it to the groom's mother. This past weekend, she went to get hers, and it's almost the same as mine, just a different color. She didn't send a picture of her dress to me; she sent it to my daughter. I asked her if she had other options and thanked her for considering a different style. Her response was, "Oh, OK. Should I go purchase a different dress? I'm not sure I have enough time, and I really love the dress that I already have." What can I do? — <i>DRESS DRAMA</i></p><p><b>DEAR DRESS DRAMA:</b> This does not have to be a problem. In fact, the "matching mothers" look is a trend that's growing in popularity, symbolizing your harmonious dedication in support of your children's union. To keep the outfits from looking too similar, choose different jewelry, accessories, hairstyles and maybe even additional layers.</p><p>Remember that on her wedding day, the focus is supposed to be on your daughter, not on you or the other mother. Please try not to take this situation as a personal slight. I doubt it was intended that way.</p><p>Dear Abby is written by Abigail Van Buren. For nearly four decades, Jeanne Phillips penned this column, which was founded in 1956 by her mother, Pauline Phillips. Contact Dear Abby at www.DearAbby.com or P.O. Box 270135, Kansas City, MO 64127.</p>

entries.title: Many birds of prey are finding utility in lamp posts, electric poles and cell towers in Chicago region
entries.summary: <p>Street lights are designed to improve safety, helping drivers see adequately at nighttime.</p><p>But they’ve also become a symbol of how some birds of prey have been adapting to the Chicago region.</p><p>Much like coyotes who have figured out how to live, hunt and grow in a metropolitan area of nearly 10 million people, certain raptors have found a way to survive here, and in some instances thrive, while enlisting the help of the towering street lamps and similar infrastructure, including cell phone towers and electric poles.</p><p>Drive long enough on Chicago-area highways or tollways and motorists may see a red-tailed hawk or a Cooper’s hawk, or at times something more exotic, perched high above the pavement on a light pole taking a rest or eyeing the medians and shoulders for the movement of a squirrel, rabbit, songbird or any other creature that could be a meal.</p><p>That means on the Kennedy Expressway near Addison Street, where a hawk has been spotted on and off for a decade, sometimes while traffic crawls below during rush hour.</p><p>Hawks have also been spotted along the Tri-State Tollway in the Rosemont area not far from O’Hare Airport, and along the Jane Addams Memorial Tollway in the outer rings of suburbia.</p><p>Within the last couple of weeks, a bald eagle was seen landing and perching atop a wooden utility pole along busy Half Day Road in the Long Grove area, causing some drivers to slow and take a look at the majestic bird until it took flight again.</p><p>In addition to hawks, amateur wildlife photographer Jeff Nelson has spotted owls, osprey and peregrine falcons on poles in the region and elsewhere in northern Illinois in recent years.</p><p>He’s captured photos of them in or near Downers Grove, La Grange, Orland Park and Chicago’s Near North and South sides, as well as elsewhere in Illinois.</p><p>The poles don’t just give some of the birds an obvious perch to hunt from over our generally flat terrain, experts say.</p><p>They also provide a spot to eat. Cook County Forest Preserve District wildlife biologist Chris Anchor said the height eliminates some of the risk that another predator will try to snatch their food. What’s more, he said, the top of the tall lights are sturdy.</p><p>“Because they don’t have teeth like we do, they have to rip things apart, so they have to find a place — a lot of times they’ll use a fence pole or a light pole as a cutting block,” Anchor said.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>Ospreys are shown by a nest atop a cell phone tower in the Wauconda area earlier this year.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Vic Berardi</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>“In 2020, only a few osprey nests were known to be on cell towers in Lake County. By 2025, at least 26 active nests have been confirmed in Lake and McHenry counties, with new ones being discovered regularly.”</p><p>Berardi added: “Many of nature’s creatures, including the osprey, are becoming increasingly dependent on human-altered environments. The upside is that we get to witness their lives up close. The downside is that we bear greater responsibility to protect and sustain the habitats they now rely on.”</p><p>A spokesperson for Verizon, the cellular carrier, said: “We currently have one site in the Chicago area with an active bird nest believed to contain ospreys.”</p><p>“If an osprey, a protected species, nests on a site, we are prohibited from climbing or performing work on the tower while it is active without an exemption from the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service to remove the birds, which is rarely granted when eggs or younglings are present. We work with biologists to ensure we care for environmental resources.”</p><p>Many birds of prey were almost wiped out in the U.S. decades ago because of, among other reasons, the use of toxic chemicals such as DDT that weakened their eggshells and then their ability to reproduce. Some species have made remarkable comebacks in the Chicago area and elsewhere, including the bald eagle, while others may be better off than before but are still struggling.</p><p>A 2025 paper by researcher Vladimir Dinets concluded: “Urban birds often develop remarkable behavioral adaptations to their complex and challenging environment.”</p><p>The research involved Dinets watching a young Cooper’s hawk hunting by a busy intersection in New Jersey.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" class="Figure-credit"><p>Robert Herguth / Sun-Times</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>“The bird seemed to understand that, whenever a human pushed the pedestrian crossing signal, a long line of cars would back up down the street,” according to a Smithsonian magazine account of the study. “The savvy creature then used the vehicles as cover to launch a sneak attack on a group of unsuspecting birds gathered in a nearby home’s front yard.”</p><p>There are dangers associated with raptors living and hunting in areas with large human populations and infrastructure, including when poles or metal towers accompany power wires and birds make the wrong kind of contact with them or other electrified components. They can be hurt or killed.</p><p>Utility companies in Illinois have been installing markings on some lines to avoid bird collisions, while putting other non-conductive objects on or near poles to lessen the chance of electrocution, officials said.</p><p>It's about helping the birds, but it’s also important in reducing outages.</p><p>Julie Heath, director of Boise State University’s Raptor Research Center, said other dangers come with birds of prey hunting near roads, including getting struck by vehicles, which has been known to especially happen with barn owls.</p><p>An Idaho study of American kestrels, a type of falcon, also found stress hormone levels were higher in the birds that lived near roadways, and they were more likely to abandon their nests, which can impact their breeding, Heath said.</p><p>Meantime, commercially available poisons used to kill rodents also remain troublesome for raptors, which may eat the poisoned creatures and then become sick or die.</p><div “They’re there, they must be good,” Heath said.</p><p>Candy Ridlbauer of the Northern Illinois Raptor & Education group near Rockford said grassy medians and shoulders along roads are nicknamed “corridor cafes” for the birds of prey given the creatures that are often there that can be eaten. But there are a lot of “hazards being that close to roadways," principally cars and trucks, she said.</p><p>Jacques Nuzzo, executive director of the Illinois Raptor Center in downstate Decatur, said red-tailed hawks weren’t as decimated as other raptors historically, and they’re great at adapting based on need.</p><p>“Why go off and hunt in the woods when you can hunt voles all day long ... in the median of a highway,” Nuzzo said, referring to a type of rodent. “There’s tons of food there.”</p><p>“That’s the nature of a bird of prey: They’re opportunists. They’re going to take advantage of any situation that arises.”</p><p>Studies have shown many songbirds in the U.S. are facing an alarming, precipitous drop in numbers, largely because of human factors, including destruction of habitat, pollution and pesticides.</p><p>Locally, even the number of American robins seems to be declining, while more of those birds appear to be staying put longer in the region rather than migrating in the colder months.</p><p>Many raptors in Illinois have seen their numbers rise since the 1960s as the worst toxins were phased out, even if some of the bird Here, the flags wave on Navy Pier. </p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>Courtesy of Bob Faust</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Four years later, in 2021, Faust, along with the artist Nick Cave, his partner in life and art, wrapped eight CTA Green Line cars, inside and out, in the same designs as a way to encourage Chicago commuters to return to public transit after the COVID-19 pandemic.</p><p>Then, last spring, Faust connected with Good Chaos, a Chicago studio and arts incubator, to revive the idea once again. This time, the images were applied to flags. The effort is a response to his sense that the American flag has increasingly been claimed as a symbol of the political right.</p><p>“I have a visceral reaction now when I see the American flag,” says Faust. “I feel like, whose is that? And then I get mad because that’s our flag. It’s ours. class="Figure-content"><figcaption class="Figure-caption"><p>“They are values or morals you think about when raising your kid,” Faust said. “The ideas you hope they learn to live the power of the project lies in how easily its language can move between contexts. “What do we all have in common?” says Armour. “Bob’s tenets are things that so many people can agree upon. We want civility in our neighborhoods and communities. We want joy in our everyday lives. And we respect faith, and we need the truth.”</p><p>Since June, Good Chaos and Faust have been experimenting with that question in increasingly public settings, working with a rotating group of dancers who carry the flags in a processional performance. The first was a bombastic parade at the Obama Presidential Center in June, bringing Faust’s flags together with Nick Cave’s Soundsuits and the Kenwood Academy drum line. After that, the project traveled to a Fourth of July parade in Cincinnati, the opening parade of the Iowa State Fair, and, earlier this month, Madison Square Park in New York City.</p><p>The performances, says Faust, give the ideas a physical form. “The dancers are the ones interpreting how the tenets look in the body.”</p><p>Faust has also printed 8,000 polysilk bandanas — or “freedom flags,” as he calls them — miniature versions of the larger flags that he and the Good Chaos team distribute at the events. At Navy Pier in September, Faust had 1,000 to hand out to audiences. After the fall, wherever the bandanas go is how the project continues. That unpredictability is part of their appeal: People can wear them, transform them or simply carry them home. “If you carry a bandana with you, you’re now part of the project,” says Faust. entries.title: Woman confronts former Mormon leader she says molested her decades ago as a child at Chicago-area church
entries.summary: <p>In 2022, after memories came flooding back that she had been sexually abused decades earlier as a child at a northwest suburban Mormon congregation by church leader Wade Christofferson, Michele Boehmke decided to confront him in person.</p><p>Christofferson had long ago left the Chicago area and was living near Columbus, Ohio, where he was part of another Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints community.</p><p>Boehmke had also moved to Ohio and happened to be living 20 minutes away, so one day she said she decided to show up at his doorstep and demand accountability.</p><p>“I don’t know why you get to continue living a comfortable life with the things you’ve done,” she told him, according to an audio recording she made of the conversation that was shared with the Chicago Sun-Times. “I think the world should know who you are, who your true self is.”</p><p>“What if that’s not my true self?” Christofferson responded, according to the recording.</p><p>“How do I know?” Boehmke said. “I don’t know how many other people you’ve continued to hurt or injure or harm through all the years. Doesn’t the world deserve a warning for someone against pedophiles?”</p><p>Christofferson, a brother of an LDS apostle helping oversee the Utah-based worldwide faith system, would not directly acknowledge abuse but offered: “I fully admit I made mistakes earlier in my life, I did things that were wrong earlier in my life.”</p><p>“I’ve repented of them, haven’t repeated those, I’ve changed.”</p><p>An upcoming court hearing is expected to serve as another indication that Christofferson’s words that day were lies.</p><p>Christofferson was arrested last November on child exploitation charges related to the sexual abuse of two children in Ohio and Utah over the last few years up until late 2025, according to court records that indicate the victims were young relatives.</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-5b0000" name="image-5b0000"></a> <picture </div> </div><p>He pleaded guilty in June to coercion and enticement of a minor, which carries a sentence of at least 10 years in prison up to a life term. He’s expected to be sentenced in coming months — and Boehmke said she plans to attend and hopes to testify to help ensure Christofferson is never a free man.</p><p>While the victims in that case were apparently not preyed upon in the context of the church, Boehmke wonders nonetheless whether they could’ve been spared their horror if Mormon leaders had earlier publicized what they knew of Christofferson — that he had abused other kids in the Crystal Lake area in the 1990s and possibly the 1980s.</p><p>A church watchdog group called Floodlit says Christofferson is accused “of sexually abusing up to 12 children in Illinois,” though he hasn’t been charged with crimes in connection with those accusations, at least in part because the statute of limitations has long expired.</p><p>In the 1990s, church officials learned of at least some of the child sexual abuse in the Chicago area and as a result, “excommunicated” Christofferson, which meant stripping him of his regular status but not booting him from the church altogether, according to interviews.</p><p>He was soon “rebaptized,” restored to regular status, before moving to the Columbus area, where he took a leadership role in another Mormon congregation — which was apparently never told of his history.</p><p>But that history began coming to light earlier this year when former Woodstock resident Edward Nachel told the Mormon Stories podcast, and later the Sun-Times, he had been part of a 1990s church tribunal that dealt with accusations against Christofferson in Crystal Lake.</p><p>Nachel said he came forward after hearing about Christofferson’s arrest, and he expressed guilt that he hadn’t spoken up sooner, for decades abiding by the secrecy the church insisted on.</p><p>Boehmke noted that other church officials in Illinois, and likely beyond, knew about the troubles with Christofferson and likewise kept it secret.</p><p>“Nobody told anybody,” she said. “How did nobody think, maybe the police should know about this?”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" id="image-cb0000" name="image-cb0000"></a> Todd Christofferson.</p></figcaption><span class="line"></span><div class="Figure-credit"><p>The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints</p></div></div> </figure> </div> </div><p>Had the church “been forthcoming,” the abuse against the more recent victims perhaps “would have never” happened, Boehmke said.</p><p>“And that is a great devastation, to know that something could have been prevented.”</p><p>Christofferson’s brother, D. Todd Christofferson, is part of the church’s powerful first presidency and has acknowledged knowing “around 2020” that Wade Christofferson had abuse accusations against him. A church spokesman said earlier this year: “While he and other family members were told of Wade’s ... excommunication, he was not informed of the specific reasons and had no reason to suspect it was for abuse.”</p><p>“It was not until around 2020 that President Christofferson first learned of — through family disclosure — some of his brother’s history of abuse from thirty years earlier; he respected the adult victims’ wishes not to involve law enforcement at that time.”</p><p>“However, upon learning of a recent allegation involving a minor, President Christofferson immediately reported it to legal authorities.”</p><p>D. Todd Christofferson wouldn’t comment for this story, but Boehmke’s attorney Timothy Kosnoff said that should they decide to file a lawsuit against the church, the church leader is “not going to be able to duck” questions about what he knew about his brother “and when did he know it.”</p><p>He was "in a position where he could have stopped his brother," Kosnoff said.</p><p>The Mormon church has been mired in a child sex abuse scandal for years and has been repeatedly accused of hiding allegations and seeming to favor the abusers over the victims.</p><p>Now 47, Boehmke said after starting to come to terms several years ago with what had happened to her when she was under 10 in Crystal Lake, she told several church leaders about Wade Christofferson, to no avail.</p><p>She told them “this man is a predator,” she said. “And they ignored me.”</p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center> <div class="Enhancement-item" data-crop=""> <figure class="Figure"><a class="AnchorLink" she contacted police and filed a report against him, but McHenry County authorities determined too much time had passed to prosecute any offenses in Crystal Lake, according to police records that allude to Boehmke's recording.</p><p>She described the abuse as “assault, molestation, coercion.”</p><p>She said she’s experienced various problems as an adult she now clearly traces back to the abuse.</p><p>“My teen years were so difficult ... I continue to live with a hatred of my body ..." Boehmke said. "I was in” a relationship “for many years, and it was abusive and horrific.”</p><p>“He changed the entire trajectory of my life,” Boehmke said about Christofferson.</p><p>She made that clear when speaking to him at his front door.</p><p>“I apologize for the harm and hurt I’ve caused you over the years,” Christofferson told her, according to the audio file. “I didn’t know that this has had long-lasting lingering effects.”</p><p>To which Boehmke responded: “You didn’t know that sexually molesting a minor child would have long-lasting effects?”</p><p>Christofferson said: “I didn’t know you were — no, I didn't know you felt that way, I apologize for that.”</p><p>He confirmed to Boehmke that he was still active in his church, though he insisted he had no access to children there.</p><p>He said his wife is “aware of everything I’ve done,” to which Boehmke said, “That makes her just as equally awful.”</p><p>Christofferson replied, “That’s one way to say it, or she’s equally forgiving.”</p><p>Boehmke said, “I don’t forgive you, and I’m the victim.”</p><p>She called him “a monster” and said part of her motivation for coming forward was a concern for other children, whether in his family or his congregation.</p><p>“You may think you have to answer for these things in the next life,” Boehmke told him. “I think you need to answer right now.”</p><p>Christofferson’s wife couldn’t be reached for comment. Christofferson's attorney did not return calls and emails. A Latter-day Saints spokesman had no immediate comment. The U.S. attorney's office, which is prosecuting Christofferson in Columbus, declined comment.</p><p>Before Boehmke left Christofferson's stoop, neighborhood children can be heard on the audio recording laughing and playing nearby as birds chirped in the backdrop.</p><p>Boehmke approached a woman with those children, saying: “Hi, do you live here? entries.title: Bulls 1-2 punch of Caleb Wilson and Matas Buzelis could be 'a problem'
entries.summary: <p>The scouting report was spot on.</p><p>Early in Sunday’s game with the Bulls and the game tied, the Nuggets watched Josh Giddey kick the ball out to the right wing and into the hands of bouncy rookie Caleb Wilson.</p><p>Yes, the No. 4 overall pick has the three-pointer in his bag, but he also has a 40-inch vertical leap and the desire to put any opposing defenders on a poster.</p><p>Veteran Denver wing Aaron Gordon closed hard, and as Wilson drove around him to the right it was obvious that the pre-game film study told Gordon’s teammates to help build a wall. Cam Johnson left Isaac Okoro in the corner and Nikola Jokic collapsed off Giddey to help in front of the rim.</p><p>Call it the quick maturation of a 20-year-old.</p><p>Wilson could have crashed the wall. Heck, he could have attempted to jump over it. Why not try to put the pelt of a league MVP like Jokic in the trophy case?</p><p>Instead, he took advantage of the attention he brought, kicked the ball out to Matas Buzelis, and watched his 21-year-old teammate nail the open three-pointer.</p><p>Another reminder of what could be.</p><p>The Bulls entered training camp hoping that they have started the rebuild with two pillars to put the foundation on, and through the first three preseason games there has to be a feeling that hope has a chance for reality.</p><p>Buzelis said weeks ago that he felt like he and Wilson could be “a problem” for the rest of the league this season. Too early to flat-out declare that, but it’s at least at growing dilemma status.</p><p>Case in point came just a few minutes after the Buzelis three, as Okoro over-pursued Jamal Murray in the corner in a closeout and watched the guard go by him towards the rim. Murray meet “a problem.”</p><p>Wilson not only came off his man for the backside help but met Murray in the paint and emphatically rejected the shot attempt, doing so with his left hand.</p><p>The Nuggets ended up winning the game as a bunch of deep bench guys determined the outcome in the fourth, but Buzelis finished with 13 points, six rebounds, three assists and a block, while Wilson finished with 17 points, five assists, four rebounds and a block.</p><p>In the three preseason games – which hold very little water in the big picture – Wilson was leading the Bulls in scoring with 17.7 points per game, while Buzelis (who turned his ankle against Memphis and had a short night) was averaging 11 points in just 20 minutes per game, but also leading the team with 1.3 blocks.</p><p>A one-two punch that combined is the same age as LeBron James.</p><p>While there is still no reason for executive vice president of basketball operations Bryson Graham to sleep easy at night, he can at least feel good that there are two corner pieces to the puzzle that have been identified.</p><p>Not only have Buzelis and Wilson built chemistry off the court – evident by all the buddy videos they posted on social media this summer – but there is growing proof that there is chemistry building on the court.</p><p>Yes, they have some redundant skillsets, but NBA teams can’t have enough athletic wings that play above the rim on both ends of the floor and have shown an ability to space the floor. Coach Tiago Splitter will take five of those guys.</p><p>And the good news for the Bulls is they still have a handful of practices left and two preseason games before the regular season tips off.</p><p>Any minutes that Buzelis and Wilson can play together are important minutes. The Bulls have known that since Wilson was drafted. The rest of the league is finding that out.</p>

entries.title: Police investigating Chicago Lawn shooting that left man dead, another critically injured
entries.summary: <p>Chicago police continue to investigate a shooting that left a man dead and another critically injured Friday morning in Chicago Lawn on the South Side. </p><p>Two men, 27 and 38, were in the 6500 block of South Maplewood Avenue around 9:20 a.m. Friday when a fight broke out with someone they didn’t know, Chicago police said. </p><p>Gunfire rang out shortly after the fight began and the younger man was shot in the body while the older man was shot in the back and armpit, police said. </p><p>The younger man was taken to the University of Chicago Medical Center where he was pronounced dead, police said. His name hasn’t been released yet. </p><p>The older man was taken to the Christ Medical Center in Oak Lawn where he was in critical condition, officials said. </p><p>Area 1 detectives were investigating. </p>

href="https://newsletters.suntimes.com/t/t-l-ydthykdt-l-ij/" target="_blank" >Chicago Marathoners hit the streets with city’s support</a></h3><p></p><h5>By <a class="Link" href="https://newsletters.suntimes.com/t/t-l-ydthykdt-l-it/" target="_blank" >Pat Nabong</a>, <a class="Link" href="https://newsletters.suntimes.com/t/t-l-ydthykdt-l-ii/" target="_blank" >Brian Sandalow</a>, <a class="Link" href="https://newsletters.suntimes.com/t/t-l-ydthykdt-l-id/" target="_blank" >Zoe Singer</a> and <a class="Link" href="https://newsletters.suntimes.com/t/t-l-ydthykdt-l-ih/" target="_blank" >Amy Yee</a></h5><p>Tens of thousands of Chicago Marathon runners started their hours-long journey as the sun rose over North Columbus Drive in Grant Park.</p><p>What waited for them were 26.2 miles of some of Chicago's most distinct neighborhoods — from the Loop to Wrigleyville, down to the Near West Side, Pilsen, Bronzeville and Chinatown — and thousands of people cheering them on.</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://newsletters.suntimes.com/t/t-l-ydthykdt-l-ik/" target="_blank" >Amos Kipruto, of Kenya, finished first</a>, with an unofficial time of 2:01.09. <a class="Link" href="https://newsletters.suntimes.com/t/t-l-ydthykdt-l-iu/" target="_blank" >Hawi Feysa, of Ethiopia, repeated her win of the women’s marathon</a>, clocking in at 2:13.33 on Sunday.</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://newsletters.suntimes.com/t/t-l-ydthykdt-l-dl/" target="_blank" >Marcel Hug and Catherine Debrunner, both of Switzerland, were the race’s men’s and women’s wheelchair titleholders</a>, coming in at 1:21:34 and 1:33:16, respectively.</p><p>Runners say the 22-mile marker can be the most challenging, as the race's last leg can feel like a drag and crowds can be sparse.</p><p>That's why on 26th Street near Michigan Avenue, Chloe Wilkerson and her family were equipped with more than 6,000 water bottles, noisemakers and a DJ setup to keep runners motivated.</p><p>"We’re gonna give them as much encouragement as we can," Wilkerson told the Sun-Times.</p><p><a class="Link" href="https://newsletters.suntimes.com/t/t-l-ydthykdt-l-dr/" target="_blank" ><b>READ MORE</b></a></p><hr><p></p><h4>YOUR DAILY QUESTION ☕️</h4><p><b>What's the best sign you've ever seen at a Chicago entries.title: Passerby discovers man fatally shot in parked car in Roseland
entries.summary: <p>A passerby found a man inside a parked car, fatally shot early Monday in Roseland on the Far South Side. </p><p>The man, 33, was found with a gunshot wound to his neck around 12:35 a.m. in the 11300 block of South Edbrooke Avenue, Chicago police said. A citizen found the victim, police said. </p><p>He was taken to the Advocate Christ Medical Center in Oak Lawn where he later died, police said. </p><p>Area 2 detectives were investigating. </p>

entries.title: Barack Obama endorses Juliana Stratton for Senate in slew of midterm picks
entries.summary: <p>Declaring "if you can make it in Springfield, you can make it in Washington D.C.," former President Barack Obama on Monday endorsed Juliana Stratton for the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/elections/2026/10/01/what-to-know-us-senate-race-juliana-stratton-don-tracy-dick-durbin" >U.S. Senate seat</a> left vacant by Sen. Dick Durbin's retirement. </p><p>"Juliana Stratton is a South Sider, a mother, a caregiver, and a fighter. That’s why I was proud to endorse her first campaign for State Representative, and why I can’t wait to vote for her to be the next Senator from the great state of Illinois," Obama said in a video released by Stratton's Senate campaign. </p><p>In a rare state legislative endorsement, Obama supported Stratton's 2016 run for state representative and helped campaign for Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker and Stratton in 2018 in Urbana and Chicago. Obama has taped at least two dozen ads for Democratic candidates for governor and Senate that are expected to be released in the coming days and weeks, and he's also planning campaign stops in battleground states. </p><p>Stratton's campaign said the two last saw each other at the Obama Presidential Center dedication ceremony on June 18. He is not expected to appear in any upcoming Stratton events ahead of Election Day. </p><div class="Enhancement" data-align-center><div class="Enhancement-item"> <div class="ExternalContent-wrapper" data-embed> <iframe width="200" height="113" src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/AshasSYrQFM?feature=oembed" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen title="President Barack Obama's Message on Juliana Stratton"></iframe> </div> </div></div><p>After winning her first political campaign in 2016, Stratton — a fellow South Sider — thanked Obama in her victory speech in Bronzeville.</p><p>“I know that President Barack Obama is here in spirit,” she said. </p><p>Obama's endorsements so far have included Georgia Senate candidate Jon Ossoff, Iowa Senate candidate Josh Turek, Mississippi Senate candidate Scott Colom and Maine Senate candidate Troy Jackson. The Associated Press is reporting he'll appear alongside Michigan U.S. Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed in Detroit on Oct. 24. </p><p>He's also headlining a Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee event with Delaware Sen. Lisa Blunt Rochester this week. </p><p>Obama's endorsement mentions that Stratton "spoke out and fought back" during Operation Midway Blitz. Stratton was among a group of Illinois Democrats who <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/immigration/2026/01/17/abolish-ice-movement-illinois-democrats-delia-ramirez-juliana-stratton-patty-garcia" target="_blank" >called for abolishing ICE</a> in January 2026 — and she emphasized that message during several rallies and debates. </p><p>Stratton is endorsed by Pritzker, Durbin, Sen. Tammy Duckworth and all 14 Democratic members of the Illinois House delegation, among a slew of other Democrats. </p><p>Stratton faces Republican candidate Don Tracy, who served as the former chair of the Illinois Republican Party, and independent candidate Whitfield Harrington Jr. in the Senate race. The lieutenant governor defeated two Democratic members of Congress — U.S. Reps. Raja Krishnamoorthi and Robin Kelly — and eight other candidates in a heated March primary. </p><p>Stratton and Tracy are scheduled to participate in a WTTW forum next week. </p>

entries.title: Lake Street bridge closes to CTA Green, Pink lines starting Tuesday
entries.summary: <p>The Lake Street bridge over the Chicago River is set to completely close for construction Tuesday, rerouting CTA Green and Pink line trains for nearly two weeks.</p><p>Shuttle buses will run between the Clark/Lake and Clinton stations for the length of the closure, through Oct. 26, according to the transit authority.</p><p>Pink Line trains won't run through the Loop at all. entries.title: Pope will be admitted to hospital Tuesday for lung nodule surgery, Vatican says
entries.summary: <p>VATICAN CITY (AP) — The Vatican says <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/hub/pope-leo-xiv" target="_blank" >Pope Leo XIV</a> will be admitted to the hospital on Tuesday in the late morning, ahead of surgery to remove a lung nodule discovered during recent medical tests.</p><p>The Vatican press office said the surgery will require a weeklong recovery in the hospital.</p><p>Leo revealed the discovery of the nodule during his Sunday noon prayer and said he was following doctors’ advice to have it removed. The Vatican press office said Monday that no particular issue precipitated the tests, denying Italian media reports suggesting an inflammation had prompted Leo to have the checkup.</p><p>Leo’s surgery marks the first major health event of his 17-month pontificate. It was significant because the pope himself revealed the news, in perhaps the most public way possible: at the end of his Sunday noon blessing, with thousands of people in St. Peter’s Square.</p><p>The Vatican has for centuries zealously guarded the pope’s health and has often sent out confusing information, or none at all, about papal illnesses. <a class="Link" href="https://apnews.com/article/vatican-pope-francis-death-psychiatry-2aecb1a0a72bf34a0c9aac1cf2197528" target="_blank" >Pope Francis tried to change that</a> by being upfront about his frailties and musing on his eventual death. But even during his pontificate, information was tightly controlled.</p><p>Leo’s decision and reveal suggested an unusual level of transparency by the American pope.</p><p>A lung nodule is a small abnormal area measuring less than 3 centimeters (1 inch) that sometimes appears on a CT scan of the chest or abdomen. Often, the scans are done to investigate trauma or a lung infection, unrelated to a lung cancer screening. A nodule can be benign or malignant, and oftentimes surgical removal is recommended to ascertain whether it is cancerous since performing a lung biopsy by needle can be difficult.</p><p>Oncologists say if the nodule turns out to be cancerous, Leo’s prognosis is “excellent” since it will have been removed at an early stage.</p><p>Unlike his predecessor Pope Francis, whose decade-long respiratory problems made him speak in a whisper, Leo tends to project his voice and frequently sings his prayers.</p>
entries.author: AP

entries.title: Michael Jordan jersey sets $14 million record for basketball memorabilia, auction house says
entries.summary: <p>MIAMI (AP) — A game-worn, autographed Michael Jordan road jersey from the 1998 NBA Finals has been privately sold for $14 million, an auction house announced Monday, calling it the highest price ever paid for a piece of basketball memorabilia.</p><p>Pennsylvania-based Hunt Auctions announced the private treaty sale and identified the buyer as Miami real estate investor Ron Firman. The red jersey is the one Jordan wore in Game 2 of that series on June 5, 1998; he and the Chicago Bulls beat the Utah Jazz that night to even the matchup at a game apiece.</p><p>Jordan and the Bulls would go on to win the series in six games, the sixth and final title of his Hall of Fame career. That 1997-98 season was the subject of the 10-episode “Last Dance” documentary series that was released in 2020.</p><p>“While Michael Jordan’s importance within the sports memorabilia marketplace has long been established it has now escalated to an elite asset class more typically reserved for iconic works of art,” said David Hunt, president of Hunt Auctions. “We are very pleased to have been able to facilitate this historic sale which serves as another benchmark for our industry.”</p><p>The $14 million price would be the second-biggest known cost for a game-worn jersey, behind the $24.12 million paid in 2024 for the jersey worn by Babe Ruth of the New York Yankees when he hit the “called shot” home run against the Chicago Cubs at Wrigley Field in Game 3 of the 1932 World Series.</p><p>This sale becomes at least the third time a Jordan jersey from that 1998 finals has fetched at least $10 million. A jersey from Game 1 was sold at auction for about $10.1 million in 2022 and <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bulls/2026/09/30/michael-jordans-last-dance-jersey-sells-for-record-12-26-million" >a jersey from Game 3 was auctioned last month for about $12.3 million</a>.</p><p>“Michael Jordan was an incredibly talented player who is admired around the world.” Firman said in a news release distributed by the auction house. “I’m very excited about the purchase.”</p><p>The jersey that Firman purchased was originally bought from the Bulls by a private collector in 2003, Hunt said, adding that it “has remained within a succinct chain of custody having only changed hands once from the original purchaser.”</p><p>Just about anything related to the 1998 finals and Jordan’s final season with the Bulls has been the subject of massive interest in the collector space. In 2023, a pair of Air Jordan sneakers that he wore in Game 2 against the Jazz was sold by Sotheby’s for $2.2 million, touted at the time as “a new world record for the most valuable sneakers ever sold.”</p>
entries.author: AP

entries.title: What to know about funeral service for former Bears coach Mike Ditka
entries.summary: <p>The funeral mass for former <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a> coach Mike Ditka will be private, a representative for the family said. <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/09/1985-bears-championship-team-remembers-former-coach-mike-ditka-as-tip-of-the-spear" >He died Friday morning at 86.</a></p><p>The service is expected to be in Chicago, where Ditka lived at the end of his life, and as of Monday it would be limited it to family only and no details would be released. Some former players have asked to attend, but so far haven’t gotten an answer.</p><p>The family has discussed holding a celebration of life ceremony for Ditka, which would be much more open, down the road, but nothing has been scheduled. The Bears certainly will want to honor him as well and likely will do a tribute at their next home game, Oct. 22 against the Patriots.</p><p>Ditka was a Hall of Fame tight end for the franchise from 1961 through ’66 and returned as head coach in 1982. He led the team to its best run in modern history, including its only Super Bowl win in the 1985 season. Incidentally, the Bears blew out the Patriots in Super Bowl XX.</p><p>He coached the Bears until they fired him after the 1992 season, then went on to coach the Saints. He had a successful broadcasting and acting career as well.</p><p>"He drove us hard," said former cornerback Leslie Frazier, now an assistant coach for the Seahawks. "He was tough. He was hardnosed. He had in his mind what it would take for us to win a championship in Chicago and also what a Chicago Bears player should look like. He was driven.</p><p>"But at the same time, he had a big heart. I can think of so many occasions after I got done playing where I would call him up and we would just talk about different things."</p>
entries.author: Jason Lieser

entries.title: Los White Sox expresan esperanza en medio de la tristeza: ‘esto apenas comienza para nosotros’
entries.summary: <p>CLEVELAND — El clubhouse de los jugadores visitantes en el Progressive Field no estaba lleno de desesperación después de la derrota de los <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/white-sox" target="_blank" >White Sox</a> el sábado por la noche.</p><p>Sin duda había tristeza después de que el equipo perdiera su tercer juego consecutivo y dejara escapar a los Guardians, tras haber caído en los dos primeros juegos de la Serie Divisional de la Liga Americana.</p><p>Pero hubo muchos abrazos, apretones de mano y suficientes sonrisas como para contradecir ese sentimiento.</p><p>‘‘Vendrán más cosas’’, se le oyó decir con optimismo a Davis Martin.</p><p>Sean Burke cargó con una derrota inmerecida en el Juego 5, al permitir las únicas carreras con un jonrón de dos carreras de José Ramírez, quien conectó un lanzamiento que casi toca tierra. Eso no impidió que Burke fuera persona por persona en el clubhouse, agradeciendo, consolando y felicitando a sus compañeros, según correspondiera al momento.</p><p>‘‘Estos son mis hermanos’’, dijo Burke. ‘‘He jugado en muchos equipos en mi vida. Sin duda, este es el equipo favorito en el que he jugado’’.</p><p>Miguel Vargas, quien lideró a los Sox por mucho con un OPS de 1.129 en la serie, sintió lo mismo, lo que hizo más difícil tragar el final de la temporada.</p><p>‘‘Nos queremos muchísimo en este clubhouse’’, dijo. ‘‘El próximo año no va a ser lo mismo, sin duda’’.</p><p>De hecho, no lo será. Nunca lo es. Aunque gran parte del joven núcleo de los Sox parece que regresará, hay pocas garantías.</p><p>Algunos veteranos muy respetados, como Erick Fedde y Randal Grichuk, probablemente no volverán, y algunos prospectos muy bien valorados, como Caleb Bonemer y Roch Cholowsky, podrían unirse al equipo. Podría ser grandioso, pero no será esto.</p><p>‘‘Fue un grupo bastante único’’, dijo Grant Taylor. ‘‘Las contribuciones que tuvimos en el clubhouse, incluso de muchachos que no estaban en el campo, como [el lesionado] Mike Vasil, y los jugadores de rutina, simplemente pasándola bien. Éramos amigos, y eso no es algo que se obtiene de un clubhouse muchas veces’’.</p><p>‘‘Esto es muy diferente al año pasado para nosotros’’, dijo Chase Meidroth, en referencia al tercero de tres temporadas consecutivas con más de 100 derrotas. ‘‘Esta es una familia; esto es una hermandad. Queríamos ganar el uno para el otro. El año pasado no amaba el béisbol así’’.</p><p>Eso quedó en evidencia en el clubhouse después del juego. Aunque los Sox se poncharon 21 veces, estableciendo el récord de Grandes Ligas de ponches en un juego de nueve entradas —en postemporada o temporada regular—, hubo algo de positivismo y un sentido de que ‘‘les demostramos’’ entre ojos llorosos y las emociones a flor de piel.</p><p>‘‘Demostramos que somos un buen equipo’’, dijo Burke. ‘‘Durante toda la temporada creímos en nosotros cuando la gente dudaba y decía que esto no era sostenible o que era suerte. Y, más importante aún, nos demostramos a nosotros mismos que podemos hacerlo’’.</p><p>‘‘Desde el año pasado, en la segunda mitad, todos creímos que podíamos ser un equipo ganador de los playoffs’’, dijo Colson Montgomery. ‘‘Y llevamos esa mentalidad este año’’.</p><p>‘‘Nos mantuvimos unidos’’, dijo Vargas. ‘‘El ambiente en el clubhouse, todo fue increíble, compartir este tiempo con los muchachos este año. Creamos aquí una hermandad que va a durar para siempre. Es una derrota dura, pero esto apenas comienza para nosotros’’.</p><p>Quienes esperan volver, esperan ser mejores.</p><p>‘‘Todavía estoy haciendo swing a los lanzamientos de alta velocidad y a las rompientes bajas, y sigo persiguiendo pelotas que no debería’’, dijo Munetaka Murakami a través de un traductor. ‘‘Así que tengo que mejorar en toda la mecánica y en todos los aspectos del béisbol’’.</p><p>‘‘Mejoren el próximo año; nosotros estaremos listos’’, dijo Meidroth. ‘‘Estar aquí fue una buena experiencia para el próximo año, llegar al campamento y saber lo que hay que hacer para llegar a donde estamos hoy’’.</p><p>‘‘Obviamente, no fue el resultado que esperábamos en esta serie, pero este núcleo estará junto por un tiempo’’, dijo Burke. ‘‘Por muy triste que sea ahora que terminó la temporada, hay muchísimas cosas positivas que esperar y un futuro muy bueno por delante para los White Sox’’.</p><p>Los fanáticos de los Sox han escuchado eso antes, y no ha llevado a nada bueno. La historia del equipo está llena de casos aislados. En 126 temporadas, los Sox sólo han clasificado a la postemporada en temporadas consecutivas una vez, en 2020-21, y la primera temporada fue interrumpida por la pandemia.</p><p>Parece que estos Sox esperan hacerlo dos veces.</p><p>‘‘Volveremos el próximo año’’, dijo Meidroth, ‘‘y este grupo seguirá fortaleciéndose’’.</p><p>‘‘Sabemos que probablemente debimos haber hecho el trabajo’’, dijo Montgomery, ‘‘pero hay que quedarse con lo que hicimos este año. Hay mucho de qué sentirse orgullosos’’.</p><p><i>Traducido con una herramienta de inteligencia artificial (IA) y editado por los seres humanos de</i> <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/la-voz" target="_blank" ><i>La Voz Chicago</i></a><br></p>

entries.title: Every known federal prosecution in Chicago tied to Trump’s immigration blitz
entries.summary: <p>Federal prosecutors in Chicago have accused 33 known defendants of nonimmigration crimes tied to Operation Midway Blitz. Many were accused of assaulting or resisting federal agents or officers.</p><p>Two defendants have pleaded guilty. Twenty-six have been cleared. Grand jurors refused to indict at least three of the 26, and another member of that group was found not guilty at trial.</p><p>Two of the 26 saw their charges dropped through a deferred-prosecution agreement. Under the terms of such a deal, prosecutors agree to drop charges if a defendant abides by certain terms over a set period of time. entries.title: Falcons coach: Will know more about QB Michael Penix's availability vs Bears on Wednesday
entries.summary: <p>Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski said he’ll have a better idea Wednesday of whether quarterback Michael Penix will be able to play Sunday against the <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears" target="_blank" >Bears</a>.</p><p>Penix hurt his ribs during the “Sunday Night Football” overtime loss to the Ravens. Monday, Stefanski wouldn’t say whether imaging showed a break or not.</p><p>Penix was injured when he was sacked by Ravens linebacker Tavius Robinson on the fourth-to-last play of regulation Sunday. He came in for one more play, throwing an incompletion on the penultimate play of the fourth quarter. Tua Tagovailoa played overtime for the Falcons and, trailing by seven, threw an interception to end the game. He went 2-for-3 for 34 yards in the game, his first of the season.</p><p>Penix said afterward he likely would have been able to play in overtime had the Falcons started with the ball. His pain grew worse as the Ravens drove down the field to start the extra frame.</p><p>Penix, who was drafted in the first round the same year as Caleb Williams, returned in Week 3 from the third ACL surgery of his football career. He gave the Falcons a boost, beating the Packers and Saints by 21 points apiece before losing Sunday. Cooper Rush started the Falcons’ first two games, both losses, while Jack Strand appeared in relief during Game 2.</p><p>The <a class="Link" href="https://chicago.suntimes.com/bears/2026/10/11/bears-grades-packers-tyson-bagent-chicago-green-bay-lambeau-field-nfl" target="_blank" >Bears</a> have their own quarterback questions that Stefanski said he’ll monitor. Caleb Williams, Tyson Bagent or Case Keenum could start.</p><p>“We’ll see as the week goes on who’s practicing, who you can anticipate seeing … “ he said of the Bears. “But the truth is you have to prepare for an entire roster.”</p>
